name: MemMachine
version: 0.4.0 (latest tag v0.4.0 = ad8ff24; packages use setuptools-scm dynamic versions, HEAD ab96a9d of 2026-10-09 is on main after that tag)
one_line: Self-hosted FastAPI memory server (uv workspace: memmachine-server, -common, -client, plus a meta package and TS client) that keeps raw episodes as ground truth, indexes them with zero write-time LLM calls, adds a rolling short-term summary and an LLM-maintained profile (per project by default), and offers an optional LLM retrieval agent ('agent mode').

locomo.protocol: agent mode (ToolSelect/CoQ retrieval agent), gpt-4.1-mini reader, gpt-4o-mini judge, cat 1-4 = 1,540 q; SH 95.12 / MH 88.30 / T 91.59 / OD 71.88; 8.57M input tokens for the run
locomo.source: MemMachine blog 2025-12-01 'MemMachine v0.2 Delivers Top Scores and Efficiency on LoCoMo'; arXiv 2604.04853 Table 10

locomo.protocol: memory mode (plain search), gpt-4.1-mini reader, gpt-4o-mini judge, 1,540 q; SH 94.41 / MH 89.72 / T 89.10 / OD 75.00; 4.20M input tokens for the run
agent / memory mode with gpt-4o-mini reader and gpt-4o-mini judge, 1,540 q

OmniMemEval, run LOCALLY (the only locally run engine in that table), gpt-4.1-mini reader, gpt-4o-mini judge, 1,540 q, cat 5 excluded; SH 83.47 / MH 53.19 / T 71.96 / OD 57.29; 2,577 context tokens per question; MemMachine version and reranker used in that run not stated
locomo.who: independent (harness run by MemTensor, the MemOS maker)

arch.product.t: Self-hosted server (FastAPI REST v2 + MCP over stdio and HTTP) with Python and TypeScript clients; hosted MemMachine Platform also exists. uv workspace members packages/client, packages/common, packages/server; packages/meta is the umbrella 'memmachine' package.

arch.truth.t: Raw episodes are the source of truth: every add writes the verbatim message to the SQL 'episodestore' table (content, producer_id, producer_role, produced_for_id, created_at, metadata); the event backend hydrates search hits back from this table. The paper calls this 'ground-truth-preserving'.

arch.stores.t: Four layers: (1) SQL episode store; (2) short-term memory = in-process deque of recent episodes plus a rolling LLM summary persisted per session; (3) long-term episodic memory, either 'declarative' backend (VectorGraphStore: Neo4j or Nebula, Episode + Derivative nodes) or 'event' backend (SQL segment store + vector store: Qdrant, Milvus, sqlite-vec, SQLite); (4) semantic/profile memory = Postgres+pgvector 'feature' table (or relational DB + vector store).

arch.graphdb.t: Neo4j (or NebulaGraph) is used only by the legacy 'declarative' backend, and only as a vector store with DERIVED_FROM edges from derivative to episode; no entity graph. The docker-compose default profile is 'event' (Qdrant + Postgres, no graph DB), while code parse-time default for a missing backend field is still 'declarative'.

arch.scope.t: REST v2 session_key is '<org_id>/<project_id>', so episodic memory is partitioned per project, not per user or conversation; per-user separation inside a project relies on producer_id / metadata filters. Each episode is registered to up to three default semantic sets (org-wide, org-level 'User Profile' set keyed by producer_id, and project set), but with shipped defaults only the project set carries a category (profile_prompt), so the profile is per project and shared by every producer in it.

write.entry.t: POST /memories (REST v2), MemMachine.add_episodes(), MCP tool add_memory, and framework integrations (LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Strands, n8n, Dify, FastGPT, OpenClaw). target_memories selects episodic and/or semantic.

write.receipt.t: Episode store, short-term append, long-term embedding + index write and semantic enqueue run in one asyncio.gather and the call returns after all finish, so the raw and indexed episode are durable on return; the short-term summary and profile extraction are queued (background summary worker; profile poller every 2 s). The three backends are not transactional (TODO #1738), so partial failures can drift.

write.roles.t: All roles are stored verbatim in episodic memory with producer_id and producer_role. Every episode, assistant turns included, is routed to the semantic sets; by default only the project set has a category, so user and assistant turns all feed one shared project profile. Producer ('User Profile') sets get no extraction unless categories are configured; there is no user-only role filter.

write.firewall.t: No content firewall or prompt-injection defence. The only write-time guards are identity ones: '_'-prefixed user metadata keys are rejected on the event backend to stop cross-producer / cross-session impersonation, and null bytes are stripped before Postgres insertion.

write.governance.t: No PII redaction, consent or retention policy found; deletion is by episode id, session or feature id only. A payload_codec module exists with only a plaintext codec.

segment.unit.t: Long-term memory makes no write-time model call. Unit of indexing is the episode (one message): passthrough segmenter = one segment per episode by default; optional TextSegmenter splits at 500 code points. Short-term summarisation batches all episodes in the window when it overflows; profile extraction is one message at a time.

segment.rule.t: No topic or session boundary detection. Short-term memory triggers a summary when total characters (episodes + summary) exceed message_capacity (default 64,000 chars; shipped samples use 500); profile ingestion triggers when a set has at least 5 un-ingested messages or a message older than 5 minutes.

segment.measured.t: not found; no published count of write-time units or calls on LoCoMo.

extract.calls.t: Long-term episodic: 0 LLM calls (embeddings only). Short-term: 1 summary call each time the character window overflows (recursive halving on context-length errors). Profile: 1 structured LLM call per message per (set x category); with shipped defaults that is 1 call per message (project set, category 'profile'); the poller takes at most 5 un-ingested messages per set per pass. Plus a consolidation call per tag once a tag holds 20 or more features.

extract.facts.t: Profile 'features' (category, tag, feature, value) extracted by LLM into 37 fixed profile tags (for example Hobbies & Interests, Health & Wellness, Relationship & Family Context); stored with a pgvector embedding of the value. These are profile facts, not general event facts.

extract.episode.t: No per-episode narrative. The only narrative is the short-term rolling session summary (max length about message_capacity/16 words, rounded to 100), which replaces evicted turns.

extract.dates.t: Derived text carries no resolved dates: profile extraction sees only message.content (no timestamp, no speaker). Episodes keep created_at, and the event backend prefixes the timestamp in the embedded derivative text only when format options request it (default time_style None for embedding).

extract.neighbours.t: Profile update is neighbour-aware: up to 50 existing features of the same set and category are passed as OLD_PROFILE and the LLM returns ADD/DELETE commands. Episodic indexing has no neighbour awareness.

extract.failure.t: Profile: context-length errors skip and mark the message ingested; other errors leave it un-ingested for retry with exponential backoff to 60 s; missing episodes retried for a 30 s grace period then delisted. Consolidation gets up to 2 attempts (one retry) and is skipped on context-length errors. Short-term summary splits batches in half (or a single oversize episode at its midpoint) on context-window errors, otherwise keeps the old summary and logs.

graph.entities.t: not found; no entity extraction (a 'kg_experiment' branch exists, last commit 2025-12-16).
graph.entities.e: code search of packages/server (read); gh api branches/kg_experiment (read)

graph.edges.t: Only structural DERIVED_FROM edges (derivative to episode) in the declarative backend; temporal neighbours are found by ordering on (timestamp, uid), not edges. No semantic relationship edges.

graph.communities.t: No communities. Semantic-memory clustering code (ClusterManager, ClusterSplitter, cluster store) exists but is not wired into ingestion; only tests import it.
graph.communities.e: semantic_memory/cluster_manager.py:1-40; grep of packages for cluster_manager imports (read)

time.fields.t: Episodes: created_at (client-suppliable) plus SQL timestamps; segments/derivatives: _timestamp; profile features: created_at and updated_at. No valid-time or as-of reads.

time.update.t: Episodes are append-only. Profile contradictions are handled by the LLM issuing DELETE (by feature + tag) then ADD; old values are destroyed and features keep no version history. (Migration adb5618bd4ee dropped a 'history' table that held message copies, now kept in the episode store; it was not feature history.)

time.dedup.t: Profile: LLM consolidation per tag once 20+ features accumulate (keeps listed ids, merges the rest with citations carried over; the consolidation LLM may not change the tag). The SemanticService consolidation_threshold parameter is not forwarded to IngestionService, so 20 is effectively fixed. Episodic: no write-time dedup; read-time dedup by episode uid across short- and long-term results and across over-fetched segments (4x over-fetch).

derive.session.t: Short-term memory keeps recent episodes plus a rolling summary of evicted turns, built by a single background worker with dynamic batching and persisted via SessionDataManager. Default summariser 'gpt-4.1' if not configured. On re-creation only the summary is reloaded; the deque of recent episodes is not restored (open ToDo).

derive.profile.t: Semantic memory = profile of tagged features maintained by background LLM ingestion. With shipped defaults the 'profile' category runs only on the project set, so it is a per-project profile; org and producer sets exist but have no default categories. Categories, tags and set types are user-configurable via API (category templates, set types keyed by metadata).

derive.background.t: Two background loops: short-term summary worker (per session, asyncio task) and semantic ingestion poller (every 2 s, dirty sets with 5+ messages or 5-minute age, concurrent across sets and categories, purges ingested rows).

derive.forget.t: No decay or automatic forgetting; short-term eviction only removes turns from the window after summarising (they remain in the episode store and long-term index).

index.embed.t: Configurable (OpenAI, Bedrock Titan, sentence-transformers, any OpenAI-compatible); samples use text-embedding-3-small at 1,536 dims.

index.lexical.t: No persistent lexical index. BM25 is applied only as a reranker over the vector candidate set; shipped samples fuse identity (vector order) and BM25 rerankers by RRF (k=60).

index.vector.t: Declarative: Neo4j vector index (created lazily once a collection reaches 10,000 nodes; filtered ANN over-fetches 4x and falls back to exact search when it returns under 50% of the limit) or Nebula; event: Qdrant, Milvus, sqlite-vec, SQLite with hnswlib/usearch engines; profile: pgvector or a vector store.

read.rewrite.t: Only in agent mode: ChainOfQuery rewrites the query up to 3 times after an LLM sufficiency check; SplitQuery decomposes into sub-queries; RaRag (optional optimised CoQ) splits multi-hop queries with spaCy or LLM.

read.analysis.t: Agent mode only: one LLM call (ToolSelectAgent) routes the query to SplitQuery, ChainOfQuery (default) or direct MemMachine search.

read.legs.t: Parallel legs per search: short-term (most recent window episodes up to the limit, filtered, no ranking, plus the summary), long-term episodic (dense over derivatives, then neighbour expansion and rerank) and semantic profile (dense over features in each of the org, producer and project sets, top_k per set; REST default 10, the service-level default of 30 applies only when no limit is passed).

read.temporal.t: No temporal query parsing; filters on created_at/timestamp are possible through the filter language, and expand_context pulls chronological neighbours (1/3 backward, 2/3 forward).

read.traversal.t: No graph traversal; 'contextualised retrieval' walks timeline neighbours of each nucleus hit (expand_context, default 0 in the API, 3 in the LoCoMo script).

rank.fusion.t: No cross-leg fusion: episodic and semantic results are returned side by side. Within episodic, RRF fusion happens only if the configured reranker is the rrf-hybrid one (identity + BM25 in samples).

rank.rerank.t: Declarative backend requires a reranker (LTM is disabled without one); it scores each expanded context window as a string, not single hits. Providers: cross-encoder (default model cross-encoder/qnli-electra-base), Cohere (rerank-english-v3.0), Bedrock (Cohere rerank-v3.5 used in the LoCoMo config), BM25, embedder, identity, RRF. Event backend reranker optional (falls back to vector score).

rank.gate.t: Optional score_threshold (default none; direction-aware for euclidean vs cosine); agent mode's CoQ stops when the LLM judges evidence sufficient with confidence. No abstain signal to the caller.

rank.agentic.t: agent_mode=false by default; when true and a retrieval-agent LLM + reranker are configured, long-term search is run through ToolSelect -> CoQ/Split/direct with QueryPolicy max_attempts 3 and max_return_len 10,000; agent-returned episodes get a flat score of 1.0.

answer.shape.t: Engine returns structured JSON (short-term episodes + summary, long-term scored episodes, profile features). formalize_query_with_context renders <Summary>, <Episodes> as '[Weekday, Month DD, YYYY at HH:MM AM] producer: "content"' lines in chronological order, then <Query>.

answer.size.t: No token budget in the engine (limit is an episode count: API top_k default 10, internal default 20; short-term returns up to the same limit of most recent window episodes plus the summary). Measured: 2,577 context tokens per question in OmniMemEval; vendor run implies about 2,727 input tokens per question in memory mode and about 5,566 in agent mode (4.20M and 8.57M over 1,540 q).
answer.size.e: common/api/spec.py:567-590; episodic_memory.py:390; short_term_memory.py:396-443; SOTA_MEMU_MEMOS_LOCOMO.md:329 (doc); arXiv 2604.04853 Table 8 (doc, per-question division inferred)

answer.prompt.t: No answer generation in the engine; the LoCoMo script uses its own ANSWER_PROMPT (adapted from Mem0's evaluation prompt) over the formatted episodes and summary with limit 30, expand_context 3.

eval.best.t: 91.69 (agent mode, gpt-4.1-mini reader, gpt-4o-mini judge, 1,540 q), vendor-run; 91.23 memory mode.

eval.outside.t: 73.90 on OmniMemEval (same reader and judge, 1,540 q, run locally by MemTensor), a 17.3 to 17.8 point drop; multi-hop collapses to 53.19 versus 88.30 to 89.72 self-reported.

eval.models.t: Vendor: gpt-4.1-mini or gpt-4o-mini reader, gpt-4o-mini judge (llm_judge.py default, overridable by OPENAI_MODEL_NAME); embeddings text-embedding-3-small; reranker Cohere rerank-v3.5 via Bedrock in the shipped LoCoMo config; Neo4j declarative backend.

eval.rigour.t: Scripts are public and skip category 5 (cat 1-4 only); single judge pass, no confidence interval; scores depend on a paid reranker. The episodic and retrieval-agent LoCoMo harnesses build EpisodicMemory directly and accept only the declarative backend, so profile memory is not exercised there; a separate REST v2 harness (top-k 50 default, both memory types) exists, and which harness produced the published numbers is not stated. Results files are not committed.

cost.write.t: Episodic: 0 LLM calls and about 5,882 embedding inputs (one per turn with passthrough/whole-text; more with sentence chunking). Short-term: one summary call per window overflow per session (depends on message_capacity). Profile (when enabled): about 5,882 extraction calls with shipped defaults (one per message, project set only) plus consolidation calls; each extra set with a category adds another 5,882. Not used in the vendor LoCoMo run.

cost.read.t: Memory mode: 1 query embedding + 1 reranker call over up to min(5N,200) expanded windows, 0 LLM calls (plus 1 embedding for the profile leg). Agent mode: 1 tool-select LLM call + up to 3 CoQ sufficiency/rewrite LLM calls (or 1 split call), each round with its own search and rerank, plus a final rerank.

cost.where.t: Hosted APIs by default (OpenAI gpt-4o-mini / gpt-4.1, text-embedding-3-small, Cohere/Bedrock rerank); local options via sentence-transformers, cross-encoder, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

trust.provenance.t: Profile features carry citations (episode uids) and merges keep the union of citations; no trust score or source class. Derivatives link to episodes by DERIVED_FROM edge or segment uuid.

trust.erasure.t: delete_episodes removes the episode from the episode store, short- and long-term memory and the semantic history/citation rows, but profile features derived from it are not deleted or re-derived, so extracted facts survive erasure of their source.

trust.auth.t: No authentication or authorisation in the open-source server (only access-log and metrics middleware); the hosted Platform is separate.
trust.auth.e: server/middleware.py:17-66; grep for auth/bearer/jwt in packages/server/src (read)

trust.sharing.t: Agents share memory by writing into the same org/project session_key; producer_id / produced_for_id fields and metadata filters separate speakers. The default profile lives in the project set and is shared by every producer in the project; org-wide and producer sets are searched too but are empty unless categories are configured. No per-agent permissions.

extras.t: ToolSelectAgent routes to ChainOfQuery (iterative sufficiency check + rewrite), SplitQuery or direct search; RaragQueryAgent is an opt-in optimised multi-hop variant with spaCy decomposition (uv dependency group 'multihop').

Each nucleus hit is expanded with timeline neighbours (1/3 back, 2/3 forward) and the whole window is reranked as one string; windows are then unified best-first under an episode cap with forward-weighted proximity.
fastmcp server with add_memory, search_memory, delete_memory tools over stdio and HTTP; add writes to both episodic and profile memory.
Server, common and client are separate PyPI packages in one uv workspace with a shared lock; optional heavy deps (spaCy) kept in a dependency group rather than server install deps.

Accepted design (2026-08-31) moving the event segment store from per-tenant Postgres partitions to shared tables with incarnation-scoped tenant keys, after per-tenant DDL broke FKs and generic plans locked all partitions (HTTP 500 at 128-way concurrency).

Semantic categories, tags, set types (keyed by metadata such as producer_id) and category templates are editable via REST; ships domain prompts (CRM, health, financial analyst, writing, coding style).
Episodic memory instances per session are reference-counted and optionally kept in an LRU cache; instance_cache_size defaults to 0 (idle caching off) in code and the shipped event sample.

Over-long inputs are cut into greedy max-size chunks, requests are packed under the provider's input-count and length caps, and a text's embedding is the length-weighted average of its chunk embeddings, so no input is truncated.
Overlapping expanded segment windows are merged into connected components with a union-find, sorted chronologically and rendered once, so neighbour expansion does not repeat shared turns.
On PostgreSQL the segment store fetches backward and forward context for all seed hits in one LATERAL query over an (incarnation, timestamp, event, index, offset) index; SQLite has a separate path.
Event segment rows are keyed by a partition incarnation UUID with no FK to the registry, so deleting a session is one registry write and a queue reclaims rows asynchronously in batches.
Embedding text has no timestamp by default, but the reranker scores context strings rendered with short timestamps and producer names, so dates reach the reranker without polluting the vectors.
Derivative text embeds the producer name before the (JSON-escaped) message, so speaker identity is part of the vector.
Optional CoQ replacement: decomposes a multi-hop query (spaCy or LLM), searches hops in parallel, keeps overlapping memories, builds combined queries and returns up to 200 deduplicated episodes.
Range and vector indexes are created only once a collection or relation reaches 10,000 entities; filtered ANN uses a 4x fudge factor with exact-search fallback.
CountCachingEpisodeStorage caches per-session episode counts in memory; CachingSemanticConfigStorage caches semantic set/category config (with_config_cache default true).
Database-backed leased read-write locks for multi-replica deployments, merged 2026-10-06.
Ships an agent skill (SKILL.md plus references) for coding agents, a deployment sizing calculator (servers, GPUs, RAM, Postgres connections from a design peak) and a ChatGPT-export importer.
Evaluation scripts for LoCoMo, LongMemEval, BEAM, HotpotQA and WikiMultiHop, with LoCoMo and WikiMultiHop data bundled; judge model and endpoint taken from the environment.

token_economy.t: Small context comes from raw episodes, not compression: no write-time extraction, retrieval returns a count-capped set of verbatim turns (top_k default 10) with optional neighbour expansion, deduplicated across short- and long-term legs, plus a rolling session summary capped at about message_capacity/16 words. Profile extraction caps the existing-feature list at 50 per call and consolidates a tag once it holds 20 features. There is no token budget, so expand_context and limit directly scale context. Measured: 2,577 tokens per question (OmniMemEval); vendor claims about 80% fewer input tokens than Mem0 (4.20M vs 19.21M over 1,540 q in memory mode), agent mode roughly doubles it (8.57M).
token_economy.e: short_term_memory.py:147-156; semantic_ingestion.py:86-94,379-384; common/api/spec.py:567-570; arXiv 2604.04853 Table 8 (doc); SOTA_MEMU_MEMOS_LOCOMO.md:329 (doc)

speed.t: Write: episode store, episodic index and semantic enqueue run concurrently (asyncio.gather); embeddings batched per add; no LLM on the synchronous path; summaries and profile extraction in background workers (single summary worker per session with dynamic batching; semantic poller every 2 s with backoff to 60 s). Read: short-term, long-term and profile legs run concurrently; neighbour expansion and derivative-to-episode lookups gathered in parallel; per-phase latency histograms (Prometheus). Vendor claims up to 75% faster add/search than Mem0; no absolute latency published in the repo.

keep: Keep raw turns as ground truth and index them with zero write-time LLM calls; derive lossy layers (summary, profile) asynchronously off the hot path.
Contextualised retrieval: expand each hit with forward-weighted timeline neighbours and rerank the whole window, then fill a cap best-first.
Rolling short-term summary with a single background worker, dynamic batching and recursive halving on context-length errors.
Neighbour-aware profile updates (pass up to 50 existing features, emit ADD/DELETE) plus threshold-triggered consolidation that carries citations.
Per-phase timing histograms on encode and query, and a 4x over-fetch to survive dedup when one episode yields many segments.
avoid: Outside-harness collapse: 91.69 self-reported vs 73.90 on OmniMemEval, with multi-hop at 53.19; vendor scores depend on a paid reranker and skip profile memory.
Erasure leaves derived profile features in place after their source episode is deleted (only citation rows are removed).

No auth, no firewall, no redaction; scope is org/project and the default profile is one per project, so in a multi-user project every user's (and the assistant's) extracted facts merge into one profile; extraction is not role-filtered.
Non-transactional parallel writes to episode store, index and semantic queue (open TODO #1738) allow index/storage drift.

specialities.name: Contextualised retrieval with window reranking
specialities.t: Each vector hit becomes a nucleus expanded with timeline neighbours (1/3 back, 2/3 forward); the reranker scores the whole window as one string, and windows are unified best-first under an episode cap, trimming by forward-weighted proximity to the nucleus.

specialities.name: Zero-LLM write path over verbatim episodes
specialities.t: The synchronous add stores the raw message and its embedding only; summaries and profile extraction run in background workers, so ingest cost is embeddings and every derived layer can be rebuilt from ground truth.

specialities.name: Combined sufficiency-and-rewrite retrieval agent
specialities.t: An LLM router picks ChainOfQuery, SplitQuery or direct search; CoQ does the sufficiency check, evidence selection and next-hop rewrite in one call per round, accumulates evidence, stops at confidence 0.8 or 3 rounds, then reranks against all queries used.

specialities.name: Incarnation-scoped tenant keys
specialities.t: Segment data is keyed by a per-incarnation UUID decoupled from the registry, making tenant deletion an O(1) registry write with asynchronous purge; adopted after measured Postgres partition-lock blow-ups (HTTP 500 at 128-way concurrency).

specialities.name: Length-weighted chunk-averaged embeddings
specialities.t: Inputs longer than the embedder limit are split greedily and their chunk vectors averaged by length, with requests packed to provider caps; no silent truncation of long turns.

specialities.name: Neighbour-aware profile with cited consolidation
specialities.t: Profile updates show the LLM up to 50 existing features and take ADD/DELETE commands; once a tag holds 20 features an LLM merges them, keeps the union of source-episode citations and is not allowed to change the tag.

specialities.name: Self-healing rolling summariser
specialities.t: A single background worker drains a dynamic batch into the rolling summary; on context-window errors it halves the batch, or splits a single oversize episode at its midpoint, recursively, so no turn is dropped.
